title: I checked online and found that Python 3.13 doesn't have "typing" in it, so how do I bypass this to start pyspark?
question:
PS C:\spark-3.4.4-bin-hadoop3\bin> pyspark
Python 3.13.3 (tags/v3.13.3:6280bb5, Apr  8 2025, 14:47:33) [MSC v.1943 64 bit (AMD64)] on win32
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\spark-3.4.4-bin-hadoop3\python\pyspark\shell.py", line 31, in <module>
    import pyspark
  File "C:\spark-3.4.4-bin-hadoop3\python\pyspark\__init__.py", line 65, in <module>
    from pyspark.broadcast import Broadcast
  File "C:\spark-3.4.4-bin-hadoop3\python\pyspark\broadcast.py", line 38, in <module>
    from typing.io import BinaryIO  # type: ignore[import]
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing.io'; 'typing' is not a package
answer:
In Python3.13, The typing.io module is deprecated and cannot be directly imported.

Python 3.13 provides built-in generic types like list[int] and dict[str, int] that serve the same purpose as the deprecated typing module.

if you are still adamant on using Typing module, the alternative is collections.abc module.

example code

# deprecated
from typing import Iterable

def func1(arr: Iterable):
    return len(arr)

# alternative
from collections.abc import Iterable

def func1(arr: Iterable):
    return len(arr)

If you want to fix the typing error, you would have to go to each file and manually replace the from typing import ... with the from collections.abc import ...
